newsitem.title: USA: Cigna Q2 operating EPS up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Cigna Q2 operating EPS up 10 pct.

text.p: CIGNA Corp on Wednesday reported better-than-expected second-quarter operating income of $270 million, or $3.61 a share, helped by strength in its employee retirement and savings benefits business.
The second-quarter results compare with $252 million, or $3.28 a share a year ago. The First Call consensus estimate was for $3.44 a share.
"We are pleased with the continued earnings growth which reflects strength in all of our major business segments," Cigna chief executive Wilson Taylor said in a statement.

The much larger employee life and health benefits business, which incudes Cigna's HMO and indemnity operations, had second-quarter operating income of $126 million compared with $121 million a year ago.
HMO medical membership grew by about 280,000 covered lives, or seven percent, from June 30, 1996.
Cigna said results for the Healthsource operations, which were acquired at the end of June 1997, will be included in the third quarter results.
Operating income in individual financial services rose to $48 million in the second quarter from $42 million a year ago.
Cigna's ongoing property and casualty business had operating income of $59 million in the second quarter, up from $56 million a year ago.
The GAAP combined ratio after policyholders' dividends was 100 for the second quarter of 1997, compared with 101 for the second quarter of 1996.
The ongoing operations had $1 million of after-tax catastrophe losses for the second quarter of 1997, compared with $5 million for the same period last year.
"I remain confident that in spite of strong competition throughout the insurance industry we will see continued improvement," he said.
Second-quarter net income was $279 million, or $3.73 a share, compared with $231 million, or $3.00 a share, a year ago.
Revenues were flat at $4.7 billion in the quarter as premiums and fees also remained about constant.
Operating income in the employee retirement and savings benefits business rose to $53 million in the second quarter from $44 million a year ago.
